chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

The sun declines in the middle of Ḥazīrān at half a foot; in the middle of Tammūz at one and a half feet; in the middle of Āb at two and a half feet; in the middle of Aylūl at three and a half feet; in the middle of Tishrīn al-Awwal at five and a half feet; in the middle of Tishrīn al-Ākhir at seven and a half feet; in the middle of Kānūn al-Awwal at nine and a half feet; in the middle of Kānūn al-Ākhir at seven and a half feet; in the middle of Shubāṭ at five and a half feet; in the middle of Ādhār at three and a half feet; in the middle of Naysān at two and a half feet; in the middle of Ayyār at one and a half feet; and in the middle of Ḥazīrān at half a foot.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose position is used to determine time
key_terms.النِّصْفِ: the middle point of the month
key_terms.تِشْرِينَ الْأَوَّلِ: Tishrīn al-Awwal, a month in the Syrian calendar
key_terms.حَزِيرَانَ: Ḥazīrān, a month in the Syrian calendar
key_terms.قَدَمٍ: a foot, used here as a unit of measurement
key_terms.كَانُونَ الْأَوَّلِ: Kānūn al-Awwal, a month in the Syrian calendar

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith describe the sun’s decline through the months for determining prayer times?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a measured schedule for the sun’s decline at the midpoint of the Syrian solar months, expressed in units of feet. Its significance is tied to determining prayer-related times through observable solar positions in a jurisprudential context.
